record.paper_title: Hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin methods for second-order elliptic problems: overview, a new result and open problems
record.context_brief: Adaptivity transfer from mixed to HDG
record.original_question: Using the fact that mixed methods can be viewed as hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin methods, develop an automatic way to translate adaptive-convergence results that are known for mixed methods into corresponding adaptive-convergence results for HDG methods.

evidence.quote: Adaptivity. In the 2016 paper [ 53 ], the first convergence of an adaptive method for an HDG method was proposed. On the other hand, results of that sort for mixed methods are not difficult to find in the literature. By using that mixed methods are also HDG methods, there could be an automatic way to translate the results for the mixed methods into the corresponding results for the HDG methods.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the second-order elliptic model problem: find $u$ such that $-
abla\cdot(\kappa
abla u)=f$ in a bounded polygonal/polyhedral domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ with suitable boundary conditions, where $\kappa$ is a symmetric positive-definite coefficient and $f\in L^2(\Omega)$. Rewrite the problem in mixed form by introducing the flux $q=-\kappa
abla u$, so that $\kappa^{-1}q+
abla u=0$ and $
abla\cdot q=f$.

A hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) method on a conforming mesh $\mathcal{T}_h$ seeks $(q_h,u_h,\widehat{u}_h)\in V_h	imes W_h	imes M_h$ (with $V_h,W_h$ discontinuous polynomial spaces on elements and $M_h$ a polynomial trace space on the mesh skeleton) satisfying, for every element $K\in\mathcal{T}_h$,
$$ (\kappa^{-1}q_h,v)_K-(u_h,
abla\cdot v)_K+\langle\widehat{u}_h,v\cdot nangle_{\partial K}=0,$$
$$ -(q_h,
abla w)_K+\langle\widehat{q}_h\cdot n,wangle_{\partial K}=(f,w)_K,$$
with numerical trace $\widehat{q}_h\cdot n=q_h\cdot n+	au(u_h-\widehat{u}_h)$ on $\partial K$, together with a single-valuedness/transmission condition for $\widehat{q}_h\cdot n$ across interior faces and the boundary condition imposed on $\widehat{u}_h$. It is known that classical mixed methods (e.g., Raviart–Thomas and Brezzi–Douglas–Marini) can be recast as HDG methods through a specific choice of the local spaces $V_h,W_h,M_h$ and the stabilization parameter $	au$.

For a standard residual-type a posteriori error estimator $\eta(\mathcal{T}_h)$ together with an adaptive loop
$$ 	ext{SOLVE}	o	ext{ESTIMATE}	o	ext{MARK}	o	ext{REFINE},$$
adaptive convergence (and, in many cases, optimal convergence rates with respect to the number of degrees of freedom) is established for mixed finite element discretizations of the above problem.

Problem: Develop a general, automatic mechanism that, exploiting the identification of mixed methods as particular HDG methods, transfers known adaptive-convergence results (plain convergence and, where available, quasi-optimal rates) for mixed methods into corresponding adaptive-convergence results for HDG methods. More precisely, exhibit an explicit correspondence between the a posteriori error estimators, marking strategies, and contraction/quasi-orthogonality arguments used in the mixed setting and analogous quantities for HDG methods, so that any future adaptive-convergence theorem proved for a mixed method automatically yields an adaptive-convergence theorem for the associated HDG method.
artifact.status_search_result: No published result was found establishing a general automatic translation of adaptive convergence results from mixed methods to HDG methods. While adaptive HDG methods have been analyzed in particular cases (e.g., Cockburn–Zhang 2016 and follow-ups), a systematic transfer mechanism appears not to have been established, so the problem is considered open.
